devils-bridge.note: The Pocket Fire reached 100 percent containment and the closure area was significantly reduced effective July 31, 2026; Devil's Bridge Trail (No. 120) is no longer named in the current closure order. west-fork-oak-creek.note: Oak Creek from the West Fork drainage south to the forest boundary, including Call of the Canyon Picnic Site and West Fork Trail (No. 108), remains closed due to flood and debris-flow hazards from the Pocket Fire burn scar; the fire itself is now 100 percent contained and no longer the basis for closure here, but the separate Oak Creek temporary area closure remains in effect through August 3, 2026 at 2400 hours unless rescinded. Source: Coconino National Forest, Forest Order 03-04-06-26-002.

soldier-pass.note: The Pocket Fire reached 100 percent containment and the closure area was significantly reduced effective July 31, 2026; Soldier Pass Trail (No. 66) and trailhead are no longer named in the current closure order. Source: Coconino National Forest, Forest Order 03-04-06-26-003.

mescal-courthouse.note: The Pocket Fire reached 100 percent containment and the closure area was significantly reduced effective July 31, 2026; Mescal Trail (No. 174C) is no longer named in the current closure order, but Dry Creek Trail (No. 52) in the same Dry Creek Road corridor remains closed through September 30, 2026 unless rescinded. lava-river-cave.note: FR 171, the access road from FR 245 to the Lava River Cave trailhead, is closed to motorized vehicles for maintenance starting July 13, 2026; reaching the cave requires hiking or biking a longer unpaved approach. Source: Coconino National Forest (Forest Order 03-04-08-26-02).

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park is urging visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees. South Kaibab Trail is fully sun-exposed with no water source, and several heat-related hiker deaths have occurred on Inner Canyon trails this summer. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park is urging visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees. Several heat-related hiker deaths have occurred on Inner Canyon trails this summer, including on Bright Angel Trail. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: Stage 3 Water Restrictions remain in effect on the North Rim following an April 2026 pipeline break; all North Rim potable water is off, including Supai Tunnel, Manzanita Day Use Area, and Cottonwood Campground, so hikers must carry all water needed for the entire trail. Bottled water is sold at the North Rim General Store, 9am to 4pm daily, but not on the trail itself. A separate hard closure of the trail between Redwall Bridge and Cottonwood Campground for waterline rehabilitation is scheduled to begin October 16, 2026, ending traditional rim-to-rim hiking. Grand Canyon National Park is also urging hikers to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm due to dangerously hot conditions after several heat-related deaths this summer, including on North Kaibab Trail. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
